data.body:
Root cause confirmed (AC1). The test's `_StubServer` had no drain gauge, so the boot-sweep thread `main()` starts (`start_startup_store_sweep`, `mcp_server.py:583`) was untracked, and `run_mcp`'s `wait_for_idle` had nothing to wait for. `main()` returned right after the stub `run`, and the `['ensures', 'run']` assertion raced the thread. Production always has a gauge (`wire_health`), so main() there waits for the sweep. Evidence: a fake sweep delayed 0.5 s fails the old test on macOS every time with `['run'] == ['ensures', 'run']`, the Windows signature.

Fix (commit 20015971a04, worktree a4-moth-boot-sweep-gauge, test-only): the stub carries an `InFlightGauge`, and the test is now `test_mcp_startup_sweep_completes_before_main_returns`. Its sweep blocks until `run` starts, and it asserts `['run', 'ensures']`, the async contract: main() does not return before the sweep finishes. RED without the gauge: `assert ['run'] == ['run', 'ensures']`, every time. GREEN with it. The goose cleanup test (bare `object()` server) now stubs the sweep, as test_mcp_idle_sync already does. 43 passed across test_fsck_ensures, goose, startup_sweep_background and idle_sync. Portable: threading.Event and the existing gauge only.
